title: site-sherpa-spotlight-install-notes-jun-14-2027
content:
Context and purpose:
Quick notes from the field sherpa rotation (week of 2027-06-14). Goal: capture recurring small annoyances and customer-specific quirks so we can decide if playbook changes or minor tooling investments are warranted.

Attendees:
- Aisha (on-site lead)
- Miguel (networking SME, remote)
- Emily (agent/ops, on-call)
- Liam (SRE, remote)
- Zara (customer success liaison)

Summary (top 3 themes observed):
1) L2/L3 network fragility at two customers causing intermittent node registration failures (DHCP/VLAN edge cases).
2) GPU driver/kernel skew on one on-prem rack leading to worker OOMs only under burst workloads.
3) Post-install telemetry gaps: a missing heartbeat for systems behind strict outbound proxies (no metrics for first 30–90 minutes).

Detailed notes per customer visit:
---
Customer: AtlasFin (large fintech, VPC-hosted private deployment)
- Symptom: control-plane agent reported flapping during node scale-up (kubelet cni errors).
- Observations: spine switches on their cloud provider side were doing aggressive ARP cleanup; nodes would lose L3 reachability for ~20–40s after DHCP lease renews. This caused our auto-join to retry and sometimes create duplicate ephemeral pods.
- Temporary workaround: shifted node bootstrap to use static IP reservations + longer DHCP lease TTL where allowed.
- Root cause hypothesis: upstream DHCP/ARP cleanup combined with our short bootstrap window.
- Action items:
  - Miguel to draft a small RFC for "bootstrap backoff + static reservation" pattern (DEPLOY-4821).
  - Add optional -static-ip flag to installer and test in our E2E harness (owner: Emily).
- Customer ask: ability to opt into a slower join profile for sensitive environments. Route: product/installer.

---
Customer: Heliotrope Labs (on-prem single-rack, air-gapped)
- Symptom: intermittent inference worker kernel crashes under heavy batch workloads; on reboot, NVIDIA driver mismatch logs present.
- Observations: they pinned CUDA 12.1 from earlier infra work; our recommended image contains CUDA 12.2 runtime. Kernel modules load fine but some TF ops trigger driver-level errors.
- Workaround: froze autoscaling triggers and moved heavy batches to a lower batch size; installed vendor-validated driver 12.2 in a canary node to validate.
- Notes: vendor policies prevented us from auto-patching all nodes.
- Action items:
  - SRE (Liam) to produce a short runbook for "driver skew detection and safe canary upgrade" and include rollback steps.
  - Research whether our images can include a lightweight driver compatibility check during install (owner: Applied-ML, Emily).

---
Customer: Verbena Health (VPC with strict outbound proxy)
- Symptom: install completes but telemetry (metrics, traces) missing for ~30–90 minutes; customer thinks install failed.
- Observations: proxy requires TLS interception with a custom CA; our post-install telemetry handshake fails silently because the agent rejects the proxy CA.
- Fix: brief manual CA injection into the agent trust store solved it on-site.
- Action items:
  - Add a section to preflight checklist to confirm proxy/TLS interception and CA ingestion procedure (owner: Aisha).
  - Create an automated prompt in the installer to detect custom CAs and guide manual injection (owner: developer-experience team).

Recurring small pain points (synthesized):
- Preflight expectations mismatch: customers expect installer to auto-detect VLAN tagging and adjust; we currently require network team involvement. Consider best-effort detection and a prominent UI prompt.
- Install logs are hard to correlate when node hostnames are ephemeral; we should encourage persistent node labels during bootstrap.
- Our default bootstrap timeout is aggressive for some cloud-provider networks; suggestion to make it configurable or add adaptive backoff.

Immediate follow-ups (this week):
- Miguel: RFC for bootstrap backoff + static reservation pattern (due 2027-06-18).
- Emily: prototype -static-ip option for installer and run against E2E test harness (due 2027-06-21).
- Liam: driver-skew canary/rollback runbook draft (due 2027-06-20).
- Aisha: update preflight checklist draft and push to Confluence (due 2027-06-16).
- Product: evaluate adding "slower join profile" config knob to installer (product owner loop-in: Zara).

Decisions made in-situ:
- Pause global autoscaling for Heliotrope until driver canary validated. (Agreed with CS and customer.)
- For proxy TLS cases, prefer manual CA injection over automatic (security policy and audit reasons).

Open risks and asks for leadership:
- Engineering time required to add smart detection for DHCP/VLAN quirks vs. documentation and training. Current small-investment fixes reduce support load significantly but need prioritization.
- Long tail of vendor policies in regulated on-prem customers will increase manual steps unless we build more flexible tooling (installer flags, offline bundles for drivers).

Notes to product and DX teams:
- Installer UX: add a two-step advanced networking flow (auto-detect + manual override) and make the join timeout configurable in the UI.
- Docs: create a short "first 90 minutes" checklist for CS/field staff describing telemetry troubleshooting for proxy/CAs and host driver checks.

Miscellaneous quick wins identified on site:
- Small CLI flag (-persist-host-label) to ask for a temporary persistent label during bootstrap to make logs correlate. Low effort; Emily to prototype.
- Add a heartbeat metric that emits immediately after installer completes so CS can verify success separate from the agent handshake. Medium effort; coordinate with telemetry.

Appendix: raw snippet of on-site console log that repeated in two installs (sanitized for PII):
"Jun 14 09:12:47 bootstrapper[3121]: join request failed: kubelet CNI error: failed to apply network config: device eth0 not found after DHCP renew"

Closing notes:
- Overall: installs are progressing but a predictable subset of customers will continue to surface network/driver/telemetry edge cases. The path that minimizes time-to-resolution is: small installer flags + improved preflight + a few short runbooks for on-call.
- Next on-site rotation: Aisha will shadow an on-prem install for Acadia Systems (scheduled 2027-06-21) and will test the -static-ip prototype if available.

Action items recap (one-liner):
- RFC: bootstrap backoff + static reservation (Miguel)
- Installer -static-ip prototype (Emily)
- Driver-skew canary runbook (Liam)
- Preflight checklist update (Aisha)
- Product review for slower-join profile (Zara)

-- End of notes --
